thread:
sam: FYI, after the kernel short-seq rollout we got customer reports of p95 tail regressions for streaming <=100 tokens. I profiled host path.
lee: can you share stacks?
sam: pasted sample:
```
stack: ingress_entry -> parse_stream -> ascii_fast_check -> normalize_utf8 -> writev_batcher -> grpc_stream_write -> epoll_wait
hotspots: writev_batcher 40%, normalize_utf8 20%, grpc_stream_write 12%
```
devon: That writev_batcher is invoking syscalls per chunk. Recent change set flush_on_kv_miss=true which forces earlier flushes.
lee: two fixes: 1) reintroduce mini-aggregation (max_chunks=3, max_bytes=4kb, timeout=5ms) 2) add utf8 quick-check to skip normalize for most ascii payloads.
sam: microbench: aggregator + utf8 quick-path reduced p95 210ms -> 150ms, write syscalls -3.5x. CPU on proxy +4%.
devon: KV implications? delaying flush might increase serialization for large multi-chunk miss flows.
lee: add a bypass: if chunk_count > 8 or tenant.opt_out_kv_agg then flush immediately. Also if kv_miss && chunk_count>6 bypass.
sam: added metrics: host.streamer.writev_calls, host.preproc.normalize_ms, host.streamer.agg_bytes.
ops-bot: deploy streamer-canary -> intake-3 (5%)
ops-bot: rollout started
sam: initial 10m: p95 -19% on canary, writev_calls -3.8x, normalize_ms median 0.08ms. One heavy customer saw +6% kv latency.
devon: tighten bypass for kv_miss to chunk_count>5 for canary hosts.
ops-bot: updated canary rollout to 15%
sam: heavy-customer kv latency back to baseline; overall p95 -17%. Planning PR with microbench scripts, flame outputs, and config flags: host.streamer.agg_bytes, host.streamer.agg_chunks, host.streamer.agg_timeout_ms, host.preproc.utf8_quickcheck, host.streamer.kv_bypass_threshold. Schedule 20m follow-up tomorrow 11am.
